title: Rank and border rank of the remaining small tripartitioning tensors; R(T_{1,1,c}) = C(c+2,2)+1
statement: Let T_{a,b,c} = Σ x_A y_B z_C over all ordered partitions (A, B, C) of [n], n = a + b + c, with |A| = a, |B| = b, |C| = c. (1) Upper bounds over every field of characteristic ≠ 2 (from the partial-Fourier note): R(T_{1,2,3}) ≤ 26, R(T_{1,2,4}) ≤ 42, R(T_{1,3,3}) ≤ 56, R(T_{2,2,3}) ≤ 57, R(T_{1,1,c}) ≤ C(c+2,2)+1. (2) Lower bounds on the border rank by Koszul–Young flattenings with explicit integer projections printed in the README (ranks computed modulo every prime q ≤ 31): ≥ 21 for T_{1,2,3} and ≥ 39 for T_{2,2,3} over ℂ and in characteristic 0 or q ≤ 31; ≥ 42 for T_{1,3,3} over ℂ and in characteristic 0 or 3 ≤ q ≤ 31; and, by the ordinary flattening, ≥ 35 for T_{1,2,4} and ≥ C(c+2,2) for T_{1,1,c} over every field. (3) For all a, b, c ≥ 1 and every field F, R_F(T_{a,b,c}) ≥ C(n,c) + 1: the space of slices along the third factor contains no rank-one matrix, while a tensor that is concise in a factor of dimension r and has rank r has a rank-one slice. (4) Hence R(T_{1,1,c}) = C(c+2,2)+1 for every c ≥ 1 over every field of characteristic ≠ 2 (for c = 3: R(T_{1,1,3}) = 11), C(c+2,2) ≤ border rank(T_{1,1,c}) ≤ C(c+2,2)+1, and 36 ≤ R(T_{1,2,4}) ≤ 42. The border rank of T_{1,1,c} for c ≥ 3 is left open.
